scenes.label: Meet Meera
scenes.title: The scholarship form
scenes.caption: Meet Meera. She's twelve, and she's built a water tester that checks how cloudy the lake near his school is. Now she's applying for the Cyberpur Young Scientists scholarship. Her form is almost done. Then she reads the last line: the panel may look at applicants' public profiles for respect and integrity.
scenes.dialogue: My water tester could win this scholarship!

scenes.label: The public view
scenes.title: What a stranger would see
scenes.caption: Meera opens her profile the way a stranger would see it. Her water-tester post looks great. But further down is a comment she wrote two years ago, mocking a classmate's drawing. And a photo of her friend Aarav asleep on the bus, posted without asking. Forty people laughed at it. Meera's stomach drops.
scenes.dialogue: I forgot these were still public.

scenes.label: Digital footprint
scenes.title: Public posts leave footprints.
scenes.caption: Her brother Arjun, who's at college, sits with her. Everything you share publicly becomes your digital footprint, he says. It's searchable, anyone can screenshot it, and it can last for years. So check each post against the panel's criteria: respect and integrity. And ask one more question: did everyone in it agree to be posted?
scenes.dialogue: So it's not just what I meant, it's what they see.

scenes.label: Audit the posts
scenes.title: Every choice needs a reason.
scenes.caption: Your turn. Audit Meera's three public posts before Friday's deadline. For each one, choose keep, edit, delete and apologise, or hide it and ask. Base every choice on the evidence: respect, integrity and consent. Careful: deleting everything hides her best work too, and keeping the mocking comment fails the respect test.
scenes.dialogue: Every choice needs a reason, not a guess.

scenes.label: Before you post
scenes.title: A good footprint isn't an empty one.
scenes.caption: The audit is done. Meera also changes her privacy settings so new posts reach friends only. But settings shrink the audience; they can't stop screenshots. So before posting, she'll ask: who could see this, could it hurt someone, and did everyone agree? A good footprint isn't an empty one. It shows your best work.
scenes.dialogue: A good footprint shows your best work.

scenes.label: A happier ending
scenes.title: Shortlisted!
scenes.caption: Meera messages Rahul to say sorry, and Rahul writes back: thanks, that means a lot. Aarav asks her to keep the bus photo private, so it stays down. On Friday, the panel asks Meera all about her water tester. She's shortlisted! Her profile now tells a story she's proud of. Your turn: help Meera review more posts before they go public.
scenes.dialogue: Shortlisted! And my profile shows the real me.
